claims_about_writeup.why: The write-up file submission/contribution.md exists and matches the described content (vector construction, metrics, and reported pass@10/rank figures).

message_source_quote: Not white-bear steering (Raman): that's "think X vs don't think X" over a *named, suppressed* concept; mine is "hold a scene vs plain copy", no named concept, no suppression instruction, different family. Cosine to the white-bear direction is **0.74** (~55% shared variance), and it *outperforms* white-bear reproduced on this same split (0.784 vs 0.686).
writeup_source_quote: White-bear steering (Raman et al.) contrasts "think about X" with "do not think about X" — an awareness/suppression contrast over a named concept. This method contrasts *holding a scene in mind* with *plainly copying*, with no named concept and no suppression instruction, and is built from a different family.

differences.message_quote: every "think while writing" variant I built (think-vs-secret, think-vs-preference, relation-holding) is 0.65–0.93 cosine with white-bear. Content directions (e.g. `basic_readout` "named" − `typo` "implied") are novel but weak (~0.19), confirming the gain requires a stance, not a content readback.
differences.what: The message adds exploratory findings (other stance-variant directions collapsing onto white-bear at 0.65–0.93 cosine, and weak content directions at ~0.19 cosine) used to bolster the novelty/distinctiveness argument against the source; none of this supporting evidence appears in the write-up, which only reports the single 0.74 cosine comparison.

rationale: Both documents credit the same source, Raman et al.'s white-bear steering, describing it identically as a named/suppressed 'think X vs don't think X' contrast and distinguishing the method as a scene-holding vs plain-copying contrast with the same cosine (0.74, ~55% shared variance) and performance comparison (0.784 vs 0.686). The message additionally reports extra exploratory robustness findings (other variants collapsing toward white-bear, weak content-direction cosines) that are not present in the write-up, giving slightly more supporting detail for the novelty claim but no change in the core credit/overlap/novelty framing.
